newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Exim Bank signs $150 mln loan for Chile mine.
newsitem.headline: Japan Exim Bank signs $150 mln loan for Chile mine.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of Japan on Friday signed an agreement to extend a $150 million loan to help finance the expansion of Chile's Candelaria copper mine, the bank said in a statement.

The loan, offered on a limited recourse basis, was co-financed with the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd, Sumitomo Bank Ltd, Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd, Tokai Bank Ltd and Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, the Exim Bank said.
The $337 million expansion project will raise Candelaria's annual output of copper concentrates to 665,000 tonnes from 415,000 tonnes, with about 30 percent contained copper.

Sumitomo Metal Mining Co, which with Sumitomo Corp holds a minority 20 percent stake in the mine, will import 100,000 tonnes per year of the extra 250,000 tonnes of concentrate production, or about 30,000 tonnes of contained copper, over a 10-year period, the bank said.
Phelps Dodge Corp of the United States owns the remaining 80 percent of the mine.
Japan currently imports through long-term contracts about 200,000 tonnes per year of concentrates, or about 60,000 tonnes of recoverable copper, from Candelaria.

"Since the supply and demand of copper is predicted to be tight after 2000 due to the constant expansion of demand from Asian countries, it is extremely important for Japan to secure a long-term and stable supply of copper in the context of economic security," the Exim Bank statement said.
Exim Bank in June 1993 provided $200 million in financing to Candelaria on a limited recourse basis, together with private banks, to cover part of the mine's $584 million development cost.
